description:
The merge-integrity guard fails a merge whose result does not build and pass its tests, so the protocol that relies on it is relying on something.

## Background

`scripts/verify-commit-builds.sh` reports a cold `cargo build --workspace` of a fresh git-archive extraction as passing in 24–30 seconds, with no `sccache`, no `RUSTC_WRAPPER`, no `VERIFY_COMMIT_TARGET_DIR`, and an empty cache directory. A genuine cold build of this workspace's dependency set cannot complete in that time, so the guard may be reporting a verdict it never established.

Separately and independently observed: a merge of three branches produced a tree that did not compile, because one branch changed a function signature while another added a caller of the old form. The edits did not overlap textually, so the merge was clean. The guard reported that merge commit as building.

A build-only check would not close this even if it were sound, because a merge can compile and fail at run time — that also happened during the same container.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A merge commit whose tree fails to compile is reported as failing by the guard.
- [hard] REQ-02: A merge commit whose tree compiles but whose tests fail is reported as failing by the guard.
- [hard] REQ-03: The guard's runtime is consistent with the work it claims to perform, or the guard is removed in favour of the check that already performs that work.
- [hard] REQ-04: A self-test demonstrates REQ-01 and REQ-02 against seeded broken trees, so the guard cannot silently become vacuous again.
title: Make the merge-integrity guard fail a merge that does not build and test
